"Burnham's plan to end pension triple lock a bad idea - Swinney"
JOHN SWINNEY, First Minister of Scotland (SNP leader), reacting at Holyrood: "I think it's a bad idea. Scotland has provided free personal care for the elderly without punishing pensioners into the bargain. So I think Andy Burnham is making the same mistake that Keir Starmer made. Keir Starmer's first act was to take away winter fuel payments from pensioners, and now it seems Andy Burnham's first act is to take away the triple lock from pensioners."
At a press conference with the first ministers of Wales and Northern Ireland, Swinney had predicted Burnham would be the UK's last prime minister.
BURNHAM: "On the day my dad died, the Scottish first minister said I would be the last prime minister of the United Kingdom." He said he quoted that "not to seek sympathy nor to criticise John Swinney" and that his dad Roy "would have been the first to [defend] his right to say it".
SWINNEY in response: "maybe he should let us have a referendum and see who's right". Swinney also clarified he had offered Burnham his condolences as soon as he heard of the bereavement. Scottish government aims to hold a referendum by 2031 but needs Westminster's permission. Burnham said earlier this month such a vote would be considered when there was a clear consensus in favour, which had not been reached; he later added a referendum was "off limits".
